newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch may ask Swiss to return stolen gold - media.
newsitem.headline: Dutch may ask Swiss to return stolen gold - media.

text.p: The Netherlands may ask Switzerland to return 75,000 tonnes of gold worth over $800 million which was stolen during World War Two, Dutch news media reported on Thursday.
Media reports said the occupying Nazi German army took 145,000 tonnes of gold from the central bank and from Dutch citizens during the war and transferred it to Swiss banks.
The Netherlands was compensated for 70,000 tonnes of the gold in 1946 under an agreement reached between Switzerland and an allied commission made up of Britain, France and the United States.
Switzerland has now set up a commission of experts empowered to bypass tight bank secrecy rules to produce an historical account of Swiss commerce with Nazi Germany.
The Dutch reports said the Swiss move had encouraged the Netherlands to revive attempts to secure the rest of its gold.
NRC Handelsblad newspaper quoted a Foreign Ministry official as saying that the Swiss government and banks had thwarted previous efforts by closing ranks to maintain banking secrecy.
